intro: Most requests for wet room installation in Borthwick come from homeowners who are either adapting their bathroom for accessibility reasons or undertaking a full property renovation and want something more practical and stylish than a traditional shower enclosure. Wet rooms have become increasingly popular across Midlothian, and in a village like Borthwick — where many homes are older and bathrooms tend to be compact — the open-plan format makes excellent use of limited space. Done properly, a wet room adds real value to your home and transforms a daily routine. Done badly, it causes water damage that's expensive to put right, which is why getting the installation right from the start matters enormously.
localContext: Borthwick's housing stock presents some specific challenges for wet room installation that aren't always relevant elsewhere. The older stone-built properties and period cottages that make up a good portion of the village have thick external walls and floors that may be uneven, sloped, or constructed in ways that require more preparation before a wet room can be properly waterproofed and tanked. Solid stone floors, for example, often need significant levelling work before a linear drain can be set at the correct gradient. Modern estates in and around Borthwick are generally more straightforward, with timber-joisted floors that need specialist waterproofing membranes to prevent water ingress between floors. Borthwick sits in a moderately hard water area, which means limescale build-up on screens, drains, and fittings is a genuine consideration — a good installer will recommend fittings and drain covers that are easy to clean and less prone to scale accumulation over time.
serviceDetail: A wet room installation in Borthwick typically begins with a detailed survey of the existing bathroom space. The installer will assess the floor construction, drainage options, ceiling height, existing plumbing routes, and wall structure before anything else happens. This survey stage is critical, particularly in older Borthwick properties where surprises behind walls and under floors are common. Once a design is agreed, the existing bathroom is fully stripped. The floor is then prepared and a former or screed base is installed to create the correct gradient towards the drain — usually a fall of around 1:80. Full tanking follows, where a waterproof membrane is applied to the floor and walls, often in two or three coats with reinforcing tape at joints and corners. This tanking layer is the heart of a wet room — it's what prevents water from penetrating the structure of your home. Tiles are then laid onto the tanked surface, drain outlets are fitted and sealed, and the shower valve, screen if required, and all sanitaryware are installed. Final checks include water testing the drain, inspecting all seals, and confirming the thermostat on any thermostatic shower valve is set correctly. In a well-run installation, the whole process takes between five and ten working days depending on the size and complexity of the room.
pricing: Wet room installation in Borthwick generally sits in the range of £6,000 to £12,000 for a full project including all labour, waterproofing, tiling, and sanitaryware. Simpler installs in modern properties at the lower end of that range are realistic. Period cottages and older stone-built homes in Borthwick often push costs higher due to the extra preparation work required — levelling floors, rerouting pipework, or dealing with damp in older walls can each add several hundred pounds. The choice of tiles, drain style, and shower valve also affects the final figure significantly. Premium materials and underfloor heating will add cost but are worth considering if you're investing in a long-term renovation.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson familiar with Borthwick and the surrounding Midlothian area genuinely makes a difference for wet room work. Local installers will have worked in similar stone-built properties and period cottages before, so they're less likely to be caught off guard by what they find once a room is stripped back. They'll understand the building materials common to the area and know which waterproofing systems perform best in older structures. They're also easier to contact if a minor issue arises after the job is done — aftercare matters with wet rooms, and a local tradesperson has a reputation in the community worth protecting.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built Borthwick property?
faqs.a: Yes, but it requires careful preparation. Stone floors need levelling and solid walls may need extra tanking work. An experienced installer will survey the space first and flag any structural considerations before quoting. It's more complex than a modern build, but older Borthwick properties are converted successfully all the time.

faqs.q: How do I manage limescale on my wet room fittings given Borthwick's water supply?
faqs.a: Borthwick's moderately hard water does mean limescale is a fact of life. Specifying chrome fittings with easy-clean coatings, choosing a linear drain with removable covers, and wiping down the shower area after use all help considerably. Some homeowners in the area also install an inline scale inhibitor on the shower supply, which reduces build-up on valves and heads.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Borthwick?
faqs.a: Most wet room installations take between five and ten working days. Simpler jobs in modern homes at the lower end, and older stone-built or period properties in Borthwick that need more floor preparation or pipe rerouting at the higher end. Your installer should give you a clear programme before work starts so you can plan around having no bathroom access.

faqs.q: Do wet rooms add value to homes in Borthwick?
faqs.a: Generally yes, particularly when well-finished and properly waterproofed. In Borthwick's mix of period cottages and modern homes, a high-quality wet room is seen as a desirable feature by buyers. A poorly installed one, however, can do the opposite — water damage is a red flag during surveys. Quality of installation matters as much as the concept itself.
